title: Singapore with Toddlers: Best Parks, Playgrounds & Free Activities
excerpt: Singapore is a dream for families with toddlers — safe, clean, stroller-friendly, and packed with incredible free activities. From world-class playgrounds in the heart of the city to waterfront parks and splash pads, here's your complete guide to enjoying Singapore on a budget with little ones.
author: Family Travel Asia Team
content:
Singapore is a dream for families with toddlers — safe, clean, stroller-friendly, and packed with incredible free activities. The city-state consistently ranks as one of the best destinations in Asia for family travel, and for good reason. Public transport is a breeze, tap water is safe to drink, and there are playgrounds and green spaces on nearly every corner. Best of all, many of the best toddler-friendly attractions in Singapore are completely free. Here's our complete guide to the best parks, playgrounds, and free things to do with your toddler in Singapore. ## Gardens by the Bay (Outdoor Gardens — Free!) **📍 18 Marina Gardens Drive** While the cooled conservatories cost around SGD 53 (US$40) per adult, the **outdoor gardens are completely free** and absolutely spectacular for toddlers. The Supertree Grove is a jaw-dropping sight for little ones — massive vertical gardens that feel like something from another planet. The OCBC Skyway (SGD 14 / US$10.50 for adults, kids under 3 free) lets you walk between two Supertrees 22 meters up, but toddlers are often just as happy running around the base. **Best for toddlers:** The free Children's Garden (Bay East) features water play areas, sand pits, and a treehouse-style playground. Bring a change of clothes — they will get wet! **Stroller tip:** The paths are wide, flat, and perfectly paved. There are plenty of benches and shaded spots for nursing or snack breaks. Enter via the Dragonfly Bridge for the most scenic stroller route. ## East Coast Park **📍 East Coast Park Service Road** This 15-kilometer stretch of coastline is Singapore's go-to for families who want beach time, cycling, and massive playgrounds — all free. The **Marine Cove Playground**, completely renovated in recent years, is a 3,500 sqm sensory wonderland with sliding ropes, net climbers, and accessible play equipment. **Best for toddlers:** The dedicated toddler zone at Marine Cove has smaller slides, sensory panels, and rubberized flooring. There are shaded picnic shelters and Baratillo food village steps away. **Stroller tip:** The park connectors are smooth asphalt. Rent a family bike with a toddler seat from one of the many rental kiosks (~SGD 8–14 / US$6–10 per hour). ## Singapore Botanic Gardens (UNESCO World Heritage Site — Free!) **📍 1 Cluny Road** Singapore's Botanic Gardens are one of the few UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the world that are **free to enter**. The 82-hectare tropical garden is perfect for a relaxed morning with a toddler. **Best for toddlers:** The Jacob Ballas Children's Garden is a dedicated 4-hectare space for kids under 14, featuring a suspension bridge, water play area, treehouse, and edible fruit garden. **Entry is free for Singapore residents and SGD 5 (US$3.70) for tourists.** Check opening hours before visiting, as it closes on Mondays. **Stroller tip:** The main gardens are stroller-friendly, but the Children's Garden has some bark-chip paths that can be tricky. A stroller with larger wheels helps. The Swan Lake area has plenty of benches and a lovely café. ## S.E.A. Aquarium (Paid — Worth It) **📍 8 Sentosa Gateway, Siloso Beach** While not free, the S.E.A. Aquarium is arguably the best indoor toddler activity in Singapore. It's one of the largest aquariums in the world, with over 100,000 marine animals across 45 habitats. The giant Open Ocean tank with its whale sharks and manta rays mesmerizes toddlers of all ages. **Cost:** SGD 43 (US$32) for adults, SGD 33 (US$25) for children 4–12. Under 3s enter free. Book online for 10–15% discount. **Best for toddlers:** The touch pool where they can feel starfish and sea cucumbers. The immersive tunnels where fish swim overhead. The whole experience is dimly lit, cool, and quiet — perfect for toddlers who get overstimulated in loud environments. ## Free Splash Pads and Water Playgrounds Singapore is hot year-round (around 30°C / 86°F), and nothing makes a toddler happier than splashing in water. Best of all, many splash pads are completely free: - **VivoCity Sky Park** (3rd floor rooftop) — An incredible free water playground with mushroom fountains, sprinklers, and a giant bucket dump. Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, open 10am–10pm. - **Chip Bee Gardens Playground** (Holland Village area) — Retro-style playground with water play features, perfect for toddlers. - **Marina Barrage** — A sustainable water park with fountains. The rooftop also gives spectacular views of the city skyline. Free entry, Splash pad free. ## Best Free Indoor Play Spaces - **National Library (Bishan Public Library)** — The children's section has themed play corners, puzzles, and a reading garden. Free entry. Open 10am–9pm daily. - **ArtScience Museum (B1 Gallery)** — The "Sensoryscape" free exhibition lets toddlers explore textures, light, and sound. **Location:** 6 Bayfront Ave, Marina Bay Sands. - **Lorong Halus Wetland** — Free eco-playground with water play, mud kitchens, and nature trails. Great for toddlers who love getting dirty. ## Getting Around with a Toddler Singapore's MRT is a stroller-friendly dream. Every station has elevators, and priority seats are abundant. The public buses are also stroller-accessible — just look for the wheelchair symbol. A day pass costs SGD 6 (US$4.50) per adult for unlimited travel. Children under 7 ride free in MRT with an Adult Travel Card. **Best family-friendly hotels near parks:** - **Marina Bay Sands** — Connected to Gardens by the Bay, has a phenomenal infinity pool (but book two connecting rooms for space). - **Parkroyal on Pickering** — Amazing vertical garden design, family rooms, close to Chinatown and parks. - **Village Hotel Sentosa** — Right next to Sentosa beaches and playgrounds, has family suites. ## Sample Free Day Itinerary - **9:00 AM:** Breakfast at a hawker centre (SGD 5–8 / US$3.70–6 per adult, toddlers eat cheap) - **10:00 AM:** Singapore Botanic Gardens + Jacob Ballas Children's Garden - **12:30 PM:** Lunch at Botanic Gardens' Bee's Knees café (kid-friendly menu) - **2:00 PM:** Nap / quiet time near Gardens by the Bay - **4:00 PM:** Supertree Grove and free water play at Children's Garden (Bay East) - **6:00 PM:** Dinner at Satay by the Bay (family-friendly, affordable satay skewers from SGD 0.60 each) - **7:45 PM:** Garden Rhapsody light & sound show at Supertree Grove (free! Show runs 7:45pm and 8:45pm) ## Budget Summary | Item | Cost (USD) | |------|-----------| | MRT day pass (1 adult) | $4.50 | | Breakfast at hawker | $4–6 | | Botanic Gardens entry | FREE (Jacob Ballas: $3.70) | | East Coast Park | FREE | | Children's Garden (Marina Bay East) | FREE | | Garden Rhapsody show | FREE | | Dinner at Satay by the Bay | $10–15 for family | | **Total (per person)** | **~$15–25/day** | Singapore proves that you don't need to spend a fortune to have an incredible family vacation with a toddler. The city's commitment to green spaces, public amenities, and child-friendly infrastructure means that some of the best experiences cost nothing at all.
